nodes.description: ZSWIM6 is a nuclear protein that loosely associates with chromatin and co-immunoprecipitates with the repressive chromatin regulators SUZ12 and HDAC1 and with histone H3. Conditional deletion of Zswim6 in mouse ventral telencephalic progenitors broadly increases chromatin accessibility at promoters and enhancers in striatum and biases transcription toward up-regulation, consistent with a role in establishing repressive chromatin. The data are from heterologous cells and mouse knockouts; whether the human truncation produces the same deficit is untested.

nodes.description: The recurrent c.2737C>T (p.Arg913Ter) premature stop codon lies in penultimate exon 13, 48 bp upstream of the last exon junction. In lymphoblastoid cells from an affected individual the variant transcript is not degraded by nonsense-mediated decay and total ZSWIM6 mRNA is not reduced. The predicted product is a ZSWIM6 protein lacking the C-terminal Sin3-like domain; the truncated protein itself could not be detected with the available antibody, so its existence is inferred from the transcript data.
